patients.summary: Man in his early 30s with paranoid schizophrenia, repeated nonadherence and admissions, who joined in 2023 on aripiprazole and isoniazid for latent TB. Risperidone caused an oculogyric crisis in 2024, clozapine was started and abandoned, he had two police-brought ED visits and a psychiatric admission, falciparum malaria after a Uganda trip in 2025, and tuberculous meningitis in January 2026 now on continuation-phase therapy under DOT.

Wants to establish primary care for her son. Previous PCP office is closing its adult panel. He has Medicaid, verified active.
Scheduled new patient visit 9/12 at 9:00, 60 min slot.

documents.title: Prior primary care records received
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RECORDS - scanned, 34 pages, from prior primary care office. Summary abstracted by MA; originals in media tab.

Problem list as printed by sending office:
- Schizophrenia, paranoid type. Diagnosed at age 21. Followed by community psychiatry in past, gaps in follow-up. Multiple antipsychotic trials per their notes, agents not itemized.
- Latent TB infection. Interferon-gamma release assay positive 06/14/2022 (QuantiFERON). Their note same month: no cough, no weight loss, chest exam clear. Isoniazid 300 mg daily started 2022; refill history in their notes is sporadic.
- History of acute dystonic reaction to an antipsychotic (eyes rolling up). Date and drug not given in these records.
- Medication nonadherence, recurrent.

Hospital admissions noted in their 2023 encounter: psychiatric admission May 2023 and again June 2023, outside psychiatric unit. No discharge summaries included in packet.

Medications on last visit (07/2023): aripiprazole 10 mg daily; isoniazid 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Screening in packet: lipid panel and basic metabolic panel 2022, normal per their flowsheet.

MA note: recent psychiatric discharge summaries not in packet. Will ask patient/family at visit.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

29-year-old man establishing care. Came by himself; mother set up the appointment and drove him. History from patient (brief answers) and from the prior office records received 9/6.

HPI / background
Paranoid schizophrenia, diagnosed at 21. He has been on several antipsychotics over the years; he cannot name the earlier ones and the outside records do not list them. Two inpatient psychiatric stays this year, May and then June, at an outside unit. We do not have those discharge summaries. Since June he has taken aripiprazole 10 mg daily "most days." He has no psychiatrist at the moment and agrees to a referral.
Remote reaction to one of the older antipsychotics where his eyes rolled up and stuck; he remembers it as frightening. Drug not known.
Latent TB: positive QuantiFERON 6/2022 at the prior office. Isoniazid 300 mg daily was started then. He admits he takes it "on and off" and ran out a few weeks ago. No cough, fevers, night sweats or weight loss.

PMH: as above. PSH: none.
Meds: aripiprazole 10 mg daily; isoniazid 300 mg daily (lapsed).
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: a first-degree relative with schizophrenia (he did not want to say who). Mother with major depression. Father with hypertension.
SH: Lives alone in an apartment in Northampton. Started college, did not finish. Not working, on disability benefits. Never smoked. No alcohol. Denies any drug use.

ROS: negative for fever, cough, chest pain, dyspnea, abdominal pain, jaundice, dark urine, numbness or tingling.

Exam
BP 117/70, HR 67, RR 16, T 36.5, SpO2 96% RA, Wt 70.6 kg. Ht 175 cm per patient.
Gen: thin, casually dressed, sits quietly, little eye contact.
Psych: guarded, speech sparse but organized. Answers questions with a few words. Did not voice or appear to respond to hallucinations during visit. Denies thoughts of harming himself or others.
HEENT: anicteric, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no adenopathy.
Heart: RRR, no murmur. Lungs: clear bilaterally.
Abd: soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly.
Neuro: alert, oriented, moves all extremities, gait normal, no tremor or abnormal movements.
Skin: no rash.

Assessment / plan
1. Latent TB infection, on isoniazid with poor adherence. Restart isoniazid 300 mg daily; new script sent, 30 days with refills. Talked about why the full course matters and what liver symptoms to call about. Pill box suggested. Hepatic panel today. Baseline chest x-ray ordered.
2. Paranoid schizophrenia, two admissions in 2023, nonadherence history. Referral to outpatient psychiatry group placed today. Continue aripiprazole 10 mg; will refill once if needed to bridge until intake.
3. History of antipsychotic dystonic reaction. Listed as an adverse reaction on the problem list, not an allergy, since he will keep needing antipsychotics.
4. Health maintenance: HIV and hepatitis C screening today. Flu vaccine given today. COVID vaccine when the new formulation arrives.
Return 3 months, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Referral to psychiatry
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Referral: outpatient psychiatry group, routine-urgent.
Reason: 29M with paranoid schizophrenia diagnosed at 21, multiple antipsychotics in the past (agents not documented), two psychiatric admissions May and June 2023 at an outside unit, history of medication nonadherence. Currently on aripiprazole 10 mg daily. Prior acute dystonic reaction to an antipsychotic (oculogyric), drug unknown. Latent TB on isoniazid 300 mg daily. NKDA.
Request: establish ongoing psychiatric care and medication management. Mother is involved and can help with scheduling (contact via patient).

reports.text: PA and lateral views of the chest. Comparison: none available. The lungs are clear without consolidation, nodule, cavitation or effusion. No hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy. No apical scarring or calcified granuloma. Heart size and mediastinal contour are normal. Osseous structures are unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No acute cardiopulmonary process. No radiographic evidence of active or prior tuberculosis.

Your test results from this week are back and they look good.

Keep taking the isoniazid every day. Let us know if you notice yellow eyes, dark urine, belly pain or nausea.
See you in December.

RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Psychiatry intake evaluation (outside)
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY - INITIAL EVALUATION
Date of service: 01/16/2024
Referred by: primary care

Patient: Noah Nadeau, 29-year-old man. Accompanied by his mother, who supplied most of the history.

Reason for referral: established paranoid schizophrenia, recent admissions, needs ongoing care.

History: Per his mother, over roughly the last seven months, since his June discharge, his behavior has become steadily stranger. He has withdrawn from almost everyone. She often finds him muttering to himself, and he has told her the voices talk about whatever he is doing. He is certain the neighbors intend to hurt him, and he nailed boards over his apartment windows so they cannot watch him. He has lived on his own since leaving college. He gives brief, partial answers and does not dispute her account.

Psychiatric history: paranoid schizophrenia since age 21. Multiple antipsychotics in the past; specific trials not available to us. Admissions May 2023 and June 2023. Prior antipsychotic-induced oculogyric crisis, agent unknown. History of stopping medication.
Current medications: aripiprazole 10 mg daily; isoniazid 300 mg daily (latent TB, prescribed by PCP).
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Medical: latent TB infection. No surgeries.
Family: schizophrenia in a first-degree relative; his mother has major depression; his father has hypertension.
Substances: never smoker, no alcohol, denies drugs.
Social: unemployed, on disability benefits; lives alone.

Mental status: unkempt and poorly groomed. Avoids eye contact. Appears to be attending to internal stimuli at several points. Speech is understandable and goal-directed for the most part, though he loses the thread and wanders off topic now and then. Paranoid delusions regarding neighbors. Denies suicidal or homicidal ideation.
Neurological screen: no abnormalities; no tremor, rigidity or abnormal movements.

Labs (drawn today): Hb 14.2, WBC 6.8, Plt 250. Na 140, K 4.1, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, glucose 90, Ca 9.6, AST 20, ALT 18, alk phos 70, total protein 7.0, albumin 4.5, total bilirubin 0.8. Urine drug screen negative.

Assessment: relapse of paranoid schizophrenia with prominent positive symptoms and withdrawal on aripiprazole alone.
Plan:
- Add risperidone 4 mg by mouth twice daily. Continue aripiprazole 10 mg daily.
- Reviewed side effects including stiffness and abnormal eye movements; to go to ED for any eye-rolling episode.
- Mother to supervise doses where possible.
- Follow-up in 4-6 weeks, sooner if worse.

cc: primary care

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 3 days

documents.title: Emergency department record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE - regional hospital
Date of service: 01/30/2024

CC: eyes rolling up

HPI: 29-year-old man with schizophrenia and a past dystonic reaction to an antipsychotic. For the last two days he has had sudden spells where both eyes are pulled upward and stay there for several minutes, a few times each day. Psychiatry added a new antipsychotic, risperidone, about two weeks ago. No fever, headache, neck pain or trauma. No new substances.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg BID (new, started 1/16), aripiprazole 10 mg daily, isoniazid 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 124/78, HR 88, RR 16, T 36.8, SpO2 99% RA.
Alert, anxious, visibly upset by the spells. During exam, bursts of involuntary upward deviation of both eyes. Neck supple, no meningismus. Pupils equal and reactive, facial movement symmetric, other cranial nerves intact. Strength and sensation normal. No limb dystonia.

Labs: CBC, CMP and prolactin within normal limits.

ED course: diphenhydramine 50 mg IV. Eye deviation stopped within a few minutes and did not recur during 3 hours of observation.

Impression: oculogyric crisis (acute dystonic reaction) due to risperidone.
Disposition: discharged with mother. Benztropine 1 mg by mouth twice daily for 3 days. Follow up with prescribing psychiatrist this week about the regimen. Return for recurrence, difficulty swallowing or breathing.

documents.title: ED follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Mother called. Son was seen in the ED Tuesday for his eyes rolling up after the new psychiatry medicine; given a shot and sent home with benztropine for 3 days. No episodes since. Psychiatry office aware, told her they are keeping the risperidone for now.
ED record requested. Appt made with PCP 2/8.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED f/u, oculogyric crisis.

S: Seen in ED 1/30 with two days of upward eye deviation spells, about two weeks after psychiatry added risperidone 4 mg BID to aripiprazole. Got IV diphenhydramine with prompt relief, then benztropine 1 mg BID x 3 days, finished. No further spells since the ED. No stiffness, tremor, trouble swallowing. Mother says psychiatry reviewed it by phone and is continuing risperidone. He says the voices are "a little quieter."
Isoniazid: taking "most days."

O: BP 123/66, HR 61, RR 15, T 36.8, SpO2 97%, Wt 70.1 kg.
Calm, flat, brief answers. EOM full, no deviation, no nystagmus. No cogwheeling, no tremor, normal gait. Lungs clear, RRR.
ED record reviewed: CBC, CMP and prolactin normal there.

A/P:
1. Acute dystonic reaction (oculogyric crisis) due to risperidone; this is his second dystonic episode on an antipsychotic. Updated the problem list entry to include both episodes. Kept off the allergy list on purpose, since psychiatry is continuing antipsychotics. Reviewed return precautions with him and mother.
2. Schizophrenia: on risperidone 4 mg BID and aripiprazole 10 mg daily per psychiatry. Will defer regimen to them.
3. LTBI: continue isoniazid; LFTs at next visit.
RTC April.

BP 108/65, HR 71, RR 16, T 36.6, SpO2 97%, Wt 69.4 kg.
Unkempt hair, calm, minimal speech. Anicteric. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen benign. No tremor or rigidity.

Plan:
- Hepatic panel today.
- Continue isoniazid 300 mg daily; father agreed to keep the bottle in the kitchen and watch him take it.
- Psychiatry follow-up next month per their schedule.
- Physical in July with metabolic labs.

OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY - FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 05/13/2024

Seen for schizophrenia, about three months after the oculogyric crisis on risperidone. He reports that the voices are still there most days, the belief that people mean him harm has not let up, and he still keeps away from others. His family confirms he is taking the medicines; his parents now hand him the doses. He is living with his parents. He has had two psychiatric admissions within the past year (May and June 2023). He has been through several antipsychotics since the diagnosis at 21. No alcohol or drug use.

Medications: risperidone 4 mg twice daily; aripiprazole 10 mg daily; isoniazid 300 mg daily per PCP.
Allergies: NKDA.

MSE: disheveled. Affect blunted. Speech reduced in amount, with long latencies. No dystonia or abnormal movements. Denies SI/HI.

Labs: CBC, CMP, lipid panel and fasting glucose all within normal limits. Urine drug screen negative.

Assessment: paranoid schizophrenia with ongoing positive and negative symptoms on current regimen.
Plan: no changes. Continue risperidone 4 mg BID and aripiprazole 10 mg daily. Return in about 3-4 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

29M, here with mother for yearly exam. Now living with his parents.

Interval: Psychiatry follow-up 5/13, no changes. Ongoing voices and suspiciousness per mother, no dystonia since January. Isoniazid: mother supervises; she estimates he misses one or two doses a week.

ROS: no fever, sweats, cough, weight change, chest pain, dyspnea, GI or GU symptoms. No jaundice.

Meds: risperidone 4 mg BID, aripiprazole 10 mg daily (psychiatry); isoniazid 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs. Not working.

Screening: PHQ-2 1, PHQ-9 2. Denies thoughts of self-harm. Followed by psychiatry.

Exam: BP 117/67, HR 56, RR 14, T 36.5, SpO2 96%, Wt 70.5 kg, Ht 175.4 cm, BMI 22.9.
Gen: quiet, cooperative, poor eye contact.
HEENT: normal. Neck: no thyromegaly or nodes.
CV: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abd: soft, no organomegaly.
Ext: no edema. Skin: normal.
Neuro: normal gait, no tremor, no rigidity, no abnormal involuntary movements.

Antipsychotic metabolic monitoring: weight stable around 70 kg since joining; BP normal. Lipids and fasting glucose from psychiatry 5/13 reviewed: total cholesterol 157, LDL 92, HDL 52, TG 115, fasting glucose 89. A1c today.

Plan:
- A1c and hepatic panel today.
- Tdap today (no adult Tdap on record).
- Continue isoniazid with supervised dosing.
- Flu and COVID vaccines in the fall.
- Proxy form signed today for mother.
F/u 3-4 months.

documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY - FOLLOW-UP / CHANGE OF PRESCRIBER
Date of service: 09/09/2024

Jun is a 30-year-old man with roughly nine years of paranoid schizophrenia, seen today by me for the first time (transferring within the group). His father brought him because the voices have become louder and more constant over recent weeks and he has pulled further back from the family. He lives with his parents. No tobacco, alcohol or other substances.

History: repeated admissions over the years tied to poor response and to stopping medication. He has had adequate trials of both risperidone and aripiprazole, each at a therapeutic dose for six weeks or longer, with little benefit. Prior oculogyric crisis on risperidone (January 2024) and an earlier dystonic reaction on another antipsychotic.
Meds: risperidone 4 mg BID, aripiprazole 10 mg daily, isoniazid 300 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Vitals: T 36.7 C, BP 122/78, HR 76, RR 14, SpO2 98% on room air.
Exam: physical exam unremarkable; no rigidity or abnormal movements.
MSE: guarded, sparse speech, appears preoccupied; denies SI/HI.

Labs: CBC with differential, CMP and liver enzymes within normal limits; baseline ANC 4.6.

Assessment: treatment-resistant schizophrenia after two adequate antipsychotic trials.
Plan:
- Start clozapine 12.5 mg at bedtime, titrating upward over the coming weeks per schedule given to the family.
- Continue risperidone and aripiprazole for now; cross-taper to be planned once clozapine reaches a therapeutic dose.
- Weekly ANC required. Family prefers blood draws at PCP office lab; will call PCP office to arrange.
- Discussed constipation, sedation, drooling, fever and sore throat warning signs.
- Follow-up in 2-3 weeks.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE - regional hospital
Date of service: 11/06/2024

Brought in by police. 30-year-old man with paranoid schizophrenia and a history of stopping his medications, last seen by outpatient psychiatry about two months ago for worsening symptoms. Police were called to a public park where he was shouting and throwing objects. Per the officers, he has not been taking his prescribed medicines for several weeks. Family reports no prior violence.

In the ED, staff tried to calm him verbally and offered food and water without effect. He then threw chairs in the room and threatened to hurt staff.

Medications listed: risperidone 4 mg BID, aripiprazole 10 mg daily, clozapine (dose per psychiatry), isoniazid 300 mg daily; not taking any of these recently.
Allergies: no known allergies. Past dystonic reactions to antipsychotics.

Exam: BP 128/82, HR 92, RR 18, T 36.9, SpO2 98%. Agitated, pacing, responding to internal stimuli. Otherwise unremarkable exam; no rigidity, no signs of trauma.

Labs: Na 140, K 4.1, Cl 102, HCO3 24, BUN 18, Cr 1.0, glucose 98. CBC normal.

ED course: haloperidol 5 mg IM, lorazepam 2 mg IM and diphenhydramine 50 mg IM (diphenhydramine added because of his dystonia history). He settled within about 30 minutes without injury to himself or staff.

Impression: acute psychotic agitation in paranoid schizophrenia after weeks off medication.
Disposition: admitted to inpatient psychiatry, regional hospital.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Inpatient psychiatry discharge summary (outside)
documents.author: inpatient psychiatry
documents.body:
INPATIENT PSYCHIATRY - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 11/06/2024 via ED. Discharged: 11/18/2024.

Reason for admission: acute agitation and psychosis after stopping all medications, including clozapine, around mid-October.

Hospital course: received IM haloperidol, lorazepam and diphenhydramine in the ED. On the unit, risperidone (4 mg BID) and aripiprazole (10 mg daily) were restarted. Clozapine was not resumed after the lapse and is discontinued. Isoniazid 300 mg daily continued. Agitation resolved over the first several days. No dystonia during the stay. At discharge he was calm, sleeping, and denied SI/HI; hallucinations persist but are less intrusive.

Discharge diagnosis: paranoid schizophrenia, acute exacerbation in the setting of medication nonadherence.
Allergies: NKDA.

Discharge medications:
- risperidone 4 mg by mouth twice daily
- aripiprazole 10 mg by mouth daily
- isoniazid 300 mg by mouth daily
Discontinued: clozapine.

Disposition: home to parents, who will supervise medications. Outpatient psychiatry follow-up within 1-2 weeks. PCP follow-up within 1 week.

documents.title: Family call - hospitalization
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Mother called. Noah was taken to the ED by police on 11/6 and is now admitted to the inpatient psych unit at the regional hospital. She says he had stopped all his pills in October and hid it from them. She apologized for missing our calls.
Told her we will see him within a week of discharge and she should call when she has a date. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Transitional care visit. Discharged 11/18 from inpatient psychiatry (admitted 11/6 via ED after police brought him from a park). Discharge summary reviewed. Here with both parents.

Course: had stopped everything in mid-October, including clozapine, without telling the family. Treated in the ED with IM haloperidol, lorazepam and diphenhydramine. On the unit, risperidone and aripiprazole restarted; clozapine stopped and not restarted. Isoniazid continued.

Now: calmer, sleeping. Parents hand him each dose and watch. No stiffness or eye spells. Psychiatry follow-up 11/26.

Meds reconciled: risperidone 4 mg BID, aripiprazole 10 mg daily, isoniazid 300 mg daily. Clozapine removed from list.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 103/73, HR 69, RR 14, T 36.5, SpO2 96%, Wt 69.8 kg, BMI 22.7.
Calm, flat, a few words at a time. No tremor, rigidity or abnormal eye movements. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen soft, no hepatomegaly.

A/P:
1. Paranoid schizophrenia, recent admission for exacerbation after nonadherence. Supervised dosing at home. Psychiatry 11/26.
2. Clozapine discontinued: weekly CBC standing order cancelled; psychiatry office informed.
3. LTBI: isoniazid continues. Hepatic panel today.
4. Flu and COVID done in October.
RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Hepatic panel
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: AST 22, ALT 19, bili 0.6. Normal. Continue isoniazid.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy fax for isoniazid refill. Last fill 11/18 at discharge (30 tabs), so this request is on time. Risperidone and aripiprazole filled on schedule by psychiatry. Refill approved.
